items.title: Swiss German diglossia
items.claim: German-speaking Switzerland uses Swiss German dialects for everyday speech and Standard German for which contexts?

options.text: Most writing, school instruction and formal broadcasting; daily speech remains dialect

items.reveal:
Linguists describe Swiss German as a textbook case of diglossia. Standard German is used for most written and formal contexts; dialect dominates speech, including on regional television.

Swiss German varieties differ substantially from one canton to another.
items.why: A community can run two registers of a language indefinitely in parallel.

items.title: Kant's three critiques
items.claim: Immanuel Kant published three critiques. Which is correct?

options.text: Of Pure Reason (1781), of Practical Reason (1788), of the Power of Judgement (1790)
Of Logic (1700), of Politics (1750), of Religion (1800)
Of Knowledge (1850), of Art (1900), of Science (1950)

items.reveal:
Kant rarely left Konigsberg, but his work reshaped European philosophy. His 1784 essay 'Was ist Aufklarung?' coined a defining slogan: 'Sapere aude'.

The second edition of the first critique (1787) is the version standardly cited.
items.why: Philosophical revolutions can be carried out at a desk in a provincial city.

items.title: Brecht's Verfremdungseffekt
items.claim: Bertolt Brecht's theatre theory is widely translated as 'alienation effect'. What does Verfremdungseffekt specifically aim to do?

options.text: Make audiences identify completely with characters
Disrupt emotional immersion so the audience thinks critically about the social conditions depicted
Make plays as short as possible

items.reveal:
Brecht developed the concept from the late 1920s. Verfremdung is closer to 'making strange' than to ordinary alienation.

The Berliner Ensemble, founded with Helene Weigel in 1949, became its main institutional home.
items.why: Translation choices can shift the apparent meaning of a theoretical term.
